implementation_readings.reading: the proposal prose claims '9 sectors eligible from S0 start (XLC and XLRE join at ~2019-06)'; the WRITTEN rule (>= 252 sessions of adjusted history through d, counted on the symbol's own session history) gives 10 from S0 start (all but XLC; XLRE's 252nd session precedes S0) and 11 from XLC's 252nd session (2019-06-19; first affected scored slot 2019-08-05). Implemented the WRITTEN rule per the A9-F audit note ('the WRITTEN rule is deterministic and was used - the prose must not be implemented literally'). Window readers additionally fail closed on any missing session inside a read window (measure-zero on this snapshot).

'OLS of sector returns on SPY returns over the last 252 sessions through d' is implemented as: closes on master indexes [t-251, t] (the 252-session warmup window), with the OLS run on the 251 close-to-close return observations INSIDE that window. Consistent with 'warmup <= 252 sessions' and the nested 63-return correlation window. The proposal prose 'first decision uses adjusted sessions 2017-04-05..2018-04-04' counts 251 sessions on the real calendar; the written 252-session rule gives 2017-04-04..2018-04-04 at the first decision - prose not implemented literally (same precedent as the eligibility reading).

'the last 63 available adjusted close-to-close daily returns' is implemented as the 63 return observations at indexes [t-62, t] (63 returns from 64 closes), nested inside the 252-session beta window; the neighbour uses 21 returns. 'Available' is enforced by failing closed on missing observations; the pair rule (either window variance < 1e-12 -> pair excluded from BOTH sum and count; < 5 defined pairs -> sector not rankable at that decision) is implemented verbatim.

the NOMPRICE control's eligible set is the 252-session availability rule only - the 5-defined-pairs refinement is anchor/neighbour-specific (it exists only where the key is a correlation mean), per the proposal's 'same eligibility' plus rule-text structure. Each arm's skip rule (< 6 rankable sectors at d) applies to its own rankable set; both never bind on the real snapshot (measured: anchor min defined pairs 9, min eligible 10).

a 42-grid tick whose session falls in a fold gap is VOIDED and recorded, never re-timed (zero on the real snapshot); voided slots decide nothing and fill nothing. The blockwise schedule path re-inserts voided ticks at clock position so both generation paths stay byte-identical even on gap-carrying calendars.

fold-boundary FORCE_FLAT rows are costed fill events in the canonical factory path (turnover from held weights to flat, charged exactly once) - reused, not forked. No re-entry trade after the final fold's flat.

A9-F's 'legs changed per transition' is read as replaced legs (out = in = symmetric-difference/2); one replaced leg contributes 2 x (1/6) of ADJ-5 |delta_weight|. Annualized over the S0 span (1842 sessions / 252) with 43 transitions. Hedge and boundary components are hard UPPER bounds (full truncation-band flip; flat+rebuild per fold boundary) reported separately - the mid estimate (2.92/yr) is the ceiling-comparable; nothing was loosened to fit.

the module never reads disk or network; tests read the staged snapshot read-only and clamp every series to <= 2025-07-31 before any computation, and the module's calendar validator refuses any calendar extending past S0 end (structural S1 guard). Real-snapshot tests are schedule-only plus the one preregistered PnL-free identifiability measurement (ranks only: no betas, no targets, no books, no returns aggregated on real data).

no_pnl_attestation: NO strategy PnL, expectancy, profit factor, alpha, or drawdown was computed or stored anywhere in this lane. The only scored-looking numbers live on synthetic fixtures (factory value_book dummy runs, dummy synthetic PnL = minus cost drag) and the only published artifacts are structural digests (schedule digests, book digests, counts) with scored=false and real_pnl=false.
